answer: Close the nectar tap to a single inlet. Every agent enters through one audited inlet, posting a shale bond: a small, non-transferable deposit locked for thirty days and slashed on proven fraud. High-value nectar contracts then flow only in slow, per-identity drips, each drip requiring a fresh, independently checked delivery receipt. Cloning gains nothing: each clone must post its own shale bond, wait out its own lockup, and build its own receipt history before any nectar flows, while an honest agent pays once and draws steadily. Cloning multiplies cost and delay, not income.
